_comment: Parent transform x child transform: a child's transform operates in the PARENT's transformed coordinate system (css-transforms-1 §6 — transforms nest via matrix multiplication, parent matrix on the left), so parentFn on an element and childFn on its child must render exactly like the single list 'parentFn childFn'. Parents here carry NO background (only the red child paints, so fill/dominance is unambiguous) and children are centered so pivot arithmetic stays clean. ARITHMETIC (child 40x40 #e74c3c=(231,76,60); rotated bbox of w x h is (w|cos|+h|sin|) x (w|sin|+h|cos|)) — NT_Control_ChildRotate: child rotate(45deg) alone -> 40*sqrt(2) = 56.57 -> [57,57]. NT_ParentScaleX_ChildRotate: child rotates first IN THE PARENT FRAME (56.57 diamond), parent scaleX(2) then doubles screen width -> 113.14 x 56.57 -> [113,57]; a runtime that flattens the hierarchy into per-kind scalars (the Compose transform-LIST failure mode, applied cross-node) would render the fixed-order [85,85] instead. NT_ParentRotate_ChildScaleX: child scaleX(2) in the parent frame -> 80x40, parent rotate(45deg) then turns it -> (80+40)*cos45 = 84.85 square -> [85,85]; the flattened wrong answer is [113,57]. NT_ParentRotate90_ChildTranslate: parent rotate(90deg) maps the child's +x axis onto screen +y (positive CSS angles are clockwise with y-down), so translate(30px,0) moves the child 30px DOWN on screen; bbox stays [40,40] — v1 _expect cannot see the position, recorded for the v2 bbox field; the component stays for the pairwise gates and the ledger. Layout: parent 160x80, child at (60,20) = centered; content bboxes (<=113 x <=85) stay inside/near the layout box so no capture-canvas clipping is in play. No predicted red — nesting goes through separate per-node layers on all three runtimes and is expected green; the fixture exists because NOTHING exercised it, which is exactly how the transform-list hole survived.

_expect.note: no parent transform: 40x40 rotated 45deg -> 56.57 square diamond MEASUREMENT NOTE: box is the bbox of fill-band pixels, and a rotated diamond's tips are heavily antialiased, so the strict-colour bbox under-reads the geometric extent by up to ~5px (worst under scaleX(2): web itself measures 108x54 against the geometric 113x57). boxTolerance 6 absorbs that while keeping the bug renders (deltas 25-31px) unmistakable.

waive.Android: OPEN Android bug, MECHANISM MEASURED (retro R1, finding A11#0, 2026-09-04) — NOT a clip. StyleApplier chains the transform layer (step 2) OUTER to the abspos offset (step 4), so the graphicsLayer pivot was the child's LOCAL centre expressed in the PARENT frame: (20,20) instead of the child's own centre (80,40) for this 40x40 child at left:60px/top:20px (css-transforms-1 §4: the origin is 50% 50% of the element's own border box). rotate(45deg) about (20,20) sends the child centre (80,40) — rel (60,20) — to (28.3,56.6)+(20,20) = (48.3,76.6): predicted bbox x 20..76.6 / y 48.3..104.9, and the capture canvas (parent 80 + 16px pad = 96) cuts the bottom — measured Android bbox (36,65)-(91,111) in canvas px against iOS/web (69,29)-(122,82). The nested rows lose 'height' the same way (the parent transform then maps the mis-pivoted diamond), and the wave-1 'clip follows the layout slot' reading was the canvas edge catching that diamond. Fixed by conjugating every route's pivot by PositionApplier.resolvedOffset (runtimes/compose/.../transforms/TransformPivot.kt, TransformApplier.applyTransforms pivotShift); fixtures/combinations/transform-abspos-pivot.json is the size-discriminating pin (anchor-twin rows). This waiver is the red test that the fix turns stale — the device gate deletes it (exit 5).
